notes:
Account summary: Cygnus builds an enterprise search platform sold to verticals (finance, healthcare). Primary focus = massive-scale embedding index + neural reranking layer. They expect to index 100M–1B+ vectors across multi-tenant customers; objective is sub-200ms p95 for search (top-k recall+rerank pipeline) and predictable unit economics.

Key requirements / asks (from SE sessions):
- Massive ingest: continuous daily delta of 5–20M vectors; snapshot + compacting strategy required.
- Index architecture: multi-tier (hot SSD NVMe for recent vectors, cold object store for archival); want Redwood routing to hot/cold pools.
- Embedding throughput: peak ingest 2–3k v/s (batching required); online query workload ~1k qps global, mixed read/write.
- Reranking: cross-encoder style reranker for top-50 candidates, target latency budget 80–120ms for rerank stage, end-to-end p95 <= 180ms for 95% queries.
- Cost targets: aim for <$0.0005 per end-to-end search (embedding+ANN+rerank) at steady state; very sensitive to token-level pricing for rerank models. Requested Redwood Optimize guidance on batching + quantization profiles.
- Models: prefer open LLMs for reranker (quantized 7B/13B) and smaller fast encoders for embeddings; want ability to route to lighter fallback variants when load spikes.
- Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV caching for multi-turn conversational search; local per-shard cache sizing guidance needed.
- Reliability: require SLA for 99.95% uptime and automated failover policy across regions.
- Security: SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, audit logs with 1-year retention, data residency controls for EU/US partitioning.

POC notes & findings (engineer's shorthand):
- 100M index run (2/28) - Redwood baseline: ANN recall ~0.92 @k=10, rerank improved MRR by ~9%.
- Measured batch window: indexing 100M took 46 hours with current config; target is 24-36h for production. Need parallel/compaction tuning and improved ingestion batching.
- Rerank latency (single-region dev): p95 140ms using 13B quantized cross-encoder (fp16 kernels); optimistic if dedicated capacity + kernel tuning.
- Cache hit-rate observed 18% on user-similarity prefixes; expectation is 30–40% with better eviction and TTL tuning.

Commercial / procurement:
- Prefers annual reserved capacity model for predictable TCO but needs clear overage and burst pricing. Asked for a 3-tier committed capacity quote (500M / 1B / 1.5B vectors).
- Legal: redline on data residency + KMS. Compliance pack requested (SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence).

Quotes / customer language observed:
- "We need unit cost math that holds at 1B vectors — otherwise this breaks our margins."
- "If we can get predictable latency and an affordable reranker path, we can standardize on Redwood for multiple verticals."

Open questions for Redwood sales/engineering:
- Provide detailed per-component cost breakdown (embeddings, ANN storage, rerank compute) for 500M and 1B commitments.
- Recommendations for hot/cold tier sizing, compaction cadence, and snapshot strategy.
- Can Redwood guarantee p95 < 200ms for a combined ANN + rerank pipeline under 1k qps? What latency SLOs in Dedicated vs Private?
- Confirm KMS HSM support and drive instructions for customer-managed keys.
